quest.title: A Dance of Destruction
quest.description: The Balladeer has caused a series of unexpected consequences within Irminsul, and you're the only one aware of that. In order to ascertain the situation, you head off to Inazuma...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x500, Mora x22000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've made it to Amenoma Smithy!

dialogues.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
dialogues.text: Ah, it's been a while.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Pardon me. I'd like to ask a question, if I may.

dialogues.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
dialogues.text: Of course, go ahead.

response.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
response.text: Oh, now there's a question I wasn't expecting... Very well, I'll tell you what I know once more.

response.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
response.text: The once-renowned "Raiden Gokaden" comprised of five branches: Amenoma, Futsu, Isshin, Hyakume, and Senju.

response.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
response.text: The art of forging practiced by these five clans was first taught to them personally by the Almighty Shogun. Over time, the five branches diverged from one another as generations of bladesmiths honed and perfected their craft, until they became five distinct traditions.

response.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
response.text: Most of the great swordsmith clans of old have since fallen into decline, and for a long time, only the Amenoma branch kept its art alive.

response.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
response.text: But fortunately, Kaedehara Kazuha recently returned to Inazuma and took up the mantle of the Isshin Art. Now, two clans remain of the original Gokaden five.

response.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
response.text: ...If my memory serves me right, you yourself were present when he forged the Isshin blade.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh yeah, we were! Paimon remembers that now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We learned a bit about the decline of the Raiden Gokaden then, too. It seems like such a shame...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What was the reason behind their decline...?

response.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
response.text: ...*sigh* That, my friends, is a tragic tale indeed.

response.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
response.text: In fact, this was not made known to me for most of my life. All these years, I knew of those great clans' demise, but never the cause... Only recently, when the question was on my mind, did I ask Kaedehara Kazuha about this.

response.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
response.text: He told me that, as we are both heirs to a branch of the Raiden Gokaden, it was right that I should know the truth.

response.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
response.text: ...There is no harm in telling you, but I must warn you... it is a dark and sorrowful tale.

response.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
response.text: The Raiden Gokaden were the targets of a murderous rampage by a vengeful bladesmith.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Vengeful? Why?

response.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
response.text: Four hundred years ago, so I'm told, there was a catastrophic malfunction in Tatarasuna's furnace. One brave swordsmith heard the commotion and chose not to flee but he rushed to the scene, hoping to prevent a disaster...

response.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
response.text: Tatarasuna was home to a state-of-the-art forging and smelting operation in that day, and overseeing it was the Armory Officer. His surname was Niwa, though he had family ties to the Kaedehara Clan.

response.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
response.text: Knowing that they had just one chance to save countless lives, Mr. Niwa and the swordsmith leaped together into the furnace. The furnace quickly stabilized, but... neither of them made it out.

response.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
response.text: The smith's death, though heroic, dealt a devastating blow to his family's fortunes. His orphaned son was left to fend for himself, and grew up deeply resentful at the world.

response.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
response.text: In his heart, the whole of Inazuma was culpable in his tragedy. He hated the Almighty Shogun for her apparent indifference toward his father's death, and he hated everyone who had done nothing to try and save him...

response.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
response.text: Powerless and destitute, the only legacy he had to pass on to his children was his hatred. Generation after generation bore this grudge, living in utter misery.

response.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
response.text: Alas, if only the story could have ended there... But one hundred years ago, the then-head of this family reached the end of his wits... He could bear their fate no longer, and yet he could do nothing to change it.

response.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
response.text: Finally... he made a drastic decision: to take revenge on the Raiden Gokaden. In doing so, he sought to vent his pent-up anger and shake the very foundations of Inazuma's forging industry.

response.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
response.text: In his fury, he murdered indiscriminately, killing even bladesmiths from the Hyakume Clan which he belonged to. His goal was absolute: the devastation of all the Raiden Gokaden.

response.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
response.text: But when he came to the Kaedehara and Kamisato Clans, his killing spree came to an abrupt end. He failed to catch them unawares — they fought back fiercely, and they did not spare his life.

response.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
response.text: That is why the Kaedehara clan and their Isshin Art survived that day. *sigh* I suppose they were the lucky ones, under the dire circumstances.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (The legend of the Raiden Gokaden has changed. Someone else attacked the swordsmiths...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (It looks like The Balladeer did something in Irminsul, but... it seems Niwa still died.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, was there anything else you wanted to ask?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Have you seen Kazuha recently?

response.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
response.text: Kazuha? Why yes, just yesterday, in fact. We spoke for a while over some tea. He seemed well.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Phew, so he still exists... and he's the same Kazuha I know. Things don't seem as bad as I feared last night.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's all. Thank you very much.

response.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
response.text: My pleasure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't tell Paimon — there are other places you wanna visit too, right? Hehehe, your expression says it all. You can't hide anything from Paimon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: On to the next stop! Lead the way, Traveler. Paimon will be right behind you.

choices.text: Could you tell me that story one more time?

dialogues.speaker: Furuta
dialogues.text: I mean it.

dialogues.speaker: Furuta
dialogues.text: Whenever the Commissioner dines at home, Thoma always joins him. I always find myself at my most relaxed when I'm serving the two of them and listening to them chat away.

dialogues.speaker: Furuta
dialogues.text: The Commissioner has such a busy schedule that he doesn't always have the chance to take his meals at home. But, given the opportunity, he always prefers to dine here.

dialogues.speaker: Furuta
dialogues.text: They say it's because Thoma's a much better chef than most... Hehe, the Commissioner is so fond of home comforts.

dialogues.speaker: Furuta
dialogues.text: They get to talking about you sometimes too, you know. Always with a very fond tone... the way one would talk about dear old friends around whom one can truly be themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Furuta
dialogues.text: Miss Kamisato occasionally joins them as well. Whenever the whole family gets together, and they start talking about people they've met and experiences they've had, you always get a mention.

dialogues.speaker: Furuta
dialogues.text: ...It's been many years now since the late Mr. and Mrs. Kamisato passed away. Much has happened in the Kamisato Clan in that time.

dialogues.speaker: Furuta
dialogues.text: As someone who is old and gray enough to have watched their son and daughter grow up, it makes me so happy to see them meet a dependable friend whose company they enjoy so much.

dialogues.speaker: Furuta
dialogues.text: So in the future, if you ever do have the time, please know you are always very welcome at the Yashiro Commission headquarters. There will always be at least one old lady who would be delighted to have the pleasure of your company.

choices.text: Thank you very much. I will visit again.

response.speaker: Furuta
response.text: Wonderful. Hehe, thank you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon likes it here, too! Also... you were saying something about the food here being really great.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's itching to try it. We may just have to invite ourselves around for dinner sometime! ...Uh, Paimon meant we should come pay a visit again real soon! Ideally around dinnertime!

response.speaker: Furuta
response.text: Of course. You're always welcome.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, goodbye for now! We're, uhh... Where are we going next?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Tatarasuna.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Great. Goodbye, Ma'am! Don't worry, we'll see ourselves out!

response.speaker: Furuta
response.text: Alright then, take care now. Hope to see you soon!

response.speaker: Hirotatsu
response.text: Oh, are you two leaving already?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup, everything's taken care of now. Don't worry!

response.speaker: Hirotatsu
response.text: Very well, safe travels. Goodbye.

choices.text: Thank you. The people of the Kamisato Clan are very dear friends to me.

talks.objective: Go to Tatarasuna to look for clues

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Certainly do. I've researched the furnace here in some depth.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: If there's anything you want to know, just ask away!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How well do you understand the history of this area?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Like the back of my hand, haha! Make no mistake, I have been here a good many times before.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Not only that, but I've met people in Inazuma whose families used to live in Tatarasuna years ago. They said it's all true, the history here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Go on, I'm listening.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Hmm? Oh, well, uh... It's a long story, don't you know? The tale of Tatarasuna starts a long time ago.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: I'm told that its history as one of the foremost forging and smelting operations in the nation goes back around a thousand years. Still, the furnace has had a couple of serious maintenance issues along the way...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A couple? When, exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: One was just in the last few years, the other was several hundred years ago. Fun fact — I'm not the first Fontaine tech guy to come and work on it, either. There was a guy back then, too.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: They say he was a mechanic who consulted on a technology upgrade. Seems like the technological collaboration between our two nations goes back a long way, how about that!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ("Mechanic," huh? Looks like The Doctor still sabotaged the furnace, leading to all the ensuing chaos...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, weren't you gonna ask Xavier something about Tatarasuna? C'mon, ask already.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I am.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Oh... I didn't realize you two were here for a history lesson.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Me neither... Paimon doesn't know what's gotten into this one today. Feels like we've been preparing for a history exam or something...

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Hmm? What brought this on? Did you just wake up today with a sudden burning desire for historical knowledge?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Pretty much. So can I ask one more question?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Sure, go ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Have you ever heard of a "kabukimono" connected to Tatarasuna?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: A kabukimono? Hmm... No, I can't say that I have.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: I do know the word — Inazuman for those eccentric types, who always go around dressed to the nines. Just the sort of person that I'd like to meet, actually.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: But sadly, I've never had the pleasure, nor have I come across anything to do with a kabukimono where Tatarasuna is concerned.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (So there's no more kabukimono... Did The Balladeer really manage to erase himself from history completely?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (If so, he must have wanted to change the world and revert everything back to the way it was. But so far, it looks like the majority of changes have only affected himself.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you, Xavier.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Of course. Don't mention it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, we're leaving? Okay, bye, Xavier!

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Oh! You're most welcome. More than happy to help.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Farewell.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like you got all the information you're looking for.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Time to go back and see Lesser Lord Kusanali.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure. But what's up with you today...? Whatever it is, it seems like it's really troubling you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Keep your smile, Spinocrocodile! No matter what happens, Paimon will always be there for you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Come on, you gotta keep it together! Why don't you grab something to eat? You can't go facing life's challenges on an empty stomach!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, let's head off and go meet Nahida!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, don't mention it! Heehee.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Hm? Do I have company?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What kind of person comes to a place like this and just spaces out...? Let's find out — c'mon, let's ask this guy!

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Hey! I wasn't spacing out! I was pondering some problems.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure you were... Your eyes were glazed over, dude. You were a million miles away!

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Huh? Why are you making fun of me? I told you, I wasn't spacing out. I was ruminating on some problems — technological, environmental, and so forth. This is Tatarasuna, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, he said Tatarasuna. Looks like we came to the right person.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Oh? Is there something you want to know about Tatarasuna?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How should I address you?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: My name's Xavier.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you know much about Tatarasuna?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, here we are, but what are we looking for? Something? Or someone?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: #Do my eyes deceive me? Or is that {NICKNAME} and Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Xavier? What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: I was in the general area, and... now I'm in this specific area. There, that's me — so what about you two?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We have some questions, and thought you might be able to help.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're here! Um... This is the Yashiro Commission's headquarters, so...

dialogues.speaker: Hirotatsu
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, it's been a while.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hello.

dialogues.speaker: Hirotatsu
dialogues.text: If you're looking for the Commissioner and Miss Kamisato, I'm afraid your timing is unfortunate. They're not here right now...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are they out on business?

dialogues.speaker: Hirotatsu
dialogues.text: The Commissioner is out on business, and Miss Kamisato is standing in for some meetings in the Commissioner's place. If it's urgent, you're welcome to wait inside until they get back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whaddya think? Shall we go in?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you. We'll take you up on that offer.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Can we take a walk in the courtyard?

dialogues.speaker: Hirotatsu
dialogues.text: If it were anyone else, I couldn't allow it. But seeing as you're so close with the Commissioner and Miss Kamisato, I think it should be okay.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We'll be heading in then. Thanks!

dialogues.speaker: Furuta
dialogues.text: Hmm? Hello, dears... Is there something you want to say?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ma'am, can I ask you a couple of questions?

dialogues.speaker: Furuta
dialogues.text: #Hehe, of course, {NICKNAME}. Yes, I know who you are... Miss Kamisato has told me about you.

dialogues.speaker: Furuta
dialogues.text: What would you like to know?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How are the Commissioner and Miss Kamisato these days?

dialogues.speaker: Furuta
dialogues.text: Oh, they're both very well indeed. Lately, Miss Kamisato has been rather busy attending all kinds of meetings, and occasionally paying visits to some local organizations on the Commissioner's behalf...

dialogues.speaker: Furuta
dialogues.text: As for the Commissioner himself... Well, you know. Busy as ever, that much hasn't changed. Although, he does seem to be in a rather good mood these days.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So pretty much business as usual in the Yashiro Commission, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Furuta
dialogues.text: Very much so.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Ayato is still the Yashiro Commissioner, Ayaka is still the lady of the house... No changes there.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (As far as I can see, nothing's changed in the Yashiro Commission, either...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I was expecting as much, but it's still a big relief to know that the Kamisato siblings are both safe and well.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well? Got any more questions?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's all for now. Many thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Furuta
dialogues.text: You're very welcome. In fact, I would love nothing more than for you to come and visit more often, but I'm sure you must be far too busy to have time for that.

dialogues.speaker: Furuta
dialogues.text: Miss Kamisato talks about you all the time. She seems so thrilled to have you as a friend, and she's always saying how talented you are, and how much she admires you.

dialogues.speaker: Furuta
dialogues.text: I must say, many things in Inazuma seem to have taken a turn for the better since you arrived here. So you're not just Miss Kamisato's knight in shining armor, you know... you're a hero to us all.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm flattered.

dialogues.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
dialogues.text: *sigh* Whenever I'm reminded of what happened back then, it always weighs on my heart...

dialogues.speaker: Furuta
dialogues.text: Look after yourselves, won't you? Take care, now.

dialogues.speaker: Hirotatsu
dialogues.text: Safe travels. Goodbye.
